Secondly, he said, you shouldn't try to be like others because you can't drink from the same cup they drink from. The word cup means price. You can't afford their status.

Never envy anyone because you don't know what it took them to get where they are. Can you drink from the same cup they drink from? Leaders do not envy others for their positions. Then he said these words: “ To sit at my right or at my left is not mine to give.” These places belong to those to whom they were designated by my father. This means you can't even pray to Jesus to get a position. Ladies and gentlemen, listen to me. Everything is fine. Listen. Don't look at me. This is extremely important.

Then he said these words. You know that the Romans and the Greeks, I quote from the Gospel of Matthew, chapter twenty. You know that the Romans and Greeks liked to dominate each other and other people. The word "to dominate" means to possess something. That is why you call the owner "the owner of the property". It means the owner. He says that the rulers of this world like to possess people as if they were property. There are some shepherds who have the same spirit. These are my followers.

They are not your followers. The Apostle Peter says: “Shepherds, do not lord it over God’s flock.” The same word that Jesus used to describe the Romans. You don't control people. True leaders do not own people. Rather, they liberate them so that they may become great. He said: "Do not oppress people as the Romans do." Then he says these words: “It shall not be so among you.” Because in my kingdom, if you want to be a great leader, you must become a servant to all.

This means that true leaders use their talents for the benefit of all. This does not mean becoming submissive. Rather, it means dedicating yourself to your generation, and giving your talent to humanity. I'm doing that now. This is my talent. My talent is training Third World leaders. This is my talent. What is your talent? Because your talent is your field of leadership. That is why great leaders never seek followers. Rather, they strive to serve themselves and their generation.

He concludes the seminar with this statement. He says, just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve by his own life as a ransom for many.
